question.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ |

current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ | $f_X$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=-1$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.35$ | | $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.35$ | | $X=4$ | $0.1$ | $0.05$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | | $f_Y$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $-1$ $2$ $4$
$f_X(x)$ $0.35$ $0.35$ $0.3$

$y$ $0$ $1$ $3$ $5$
$f_Y(y)$ $0.3$ $0.2$ $0.2$ $0.3$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y{:}$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =(-1)\cdot 0.35+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.3 \\ & =-0.35+0.7+1.2 \\ & =1.55\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.2+3\cdot 0.2+5\cdot 0.3 \\ & =0+0.2+0.6+1.5 \\ & =2.3\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X-3Y] & =4\text{E}[X]-3\,\text{E}[Y] \\ & =4(1.55)-3(2.3) \\ & =6.2-6.9 \\ & =-0.7.\end{aligned} $$
